thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 Alert: node-bounce detected in us-west-2-gpu-pool. 7 pods restarted in the last 10m, multiple OOM/CUDA errors. Auto-escalation to #eng-oncall.

alex: seeing the same in metrics — KV cache free is slowly trending down across the pool, eviction rate spiked ~30m ago.

sana: can someone post the kubectl logs for one of the crashers? curious if it's the allocator or nv driver.

dmitri: grabbing logs now. `kubectl -n inference logs redwood-runtime-9f4b6 -c runtime`

megan: quick note — customer-facing errors: several endpoints returning 503s and a couple 504s. Support flagged 3 customers with high retry rates.

iris: paste from pod log: ```
[2026-03-15T22:02:12Z] runtime.cpp:432] Alloc failed: requested=1.2GiB available=512MiB
[2026-03-15T22:02:12Z] cuda: cuMemAlloc err=CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS code=77
[2026-03-15T22:02:12Z] killing process due to OOM
```

alex: that matches the OOM symptoms. but note: kernel shows high fragmentation on kv allocator — small free slots but not coalesced. evictions not reclaiming quickly.

sana: is this the paged-attention allocator again or a KV cache pathology? can we confirm which slab is failing?

dmitri: `gdb` dump looked like allocator metadata corrupt for slab id 12. Also saw these repeated warn messages before crash: `kv_cache: stale_page_count=1543` and `paging: slab_frag_percent=78`

megan: Ops impact summary for PMs: degradation started ~21:45 UTC, full pod crashes started ~21:54, mitigation window currently in progress. Customers impacted: acct-REDACT-113 (high latency), acct-REDACT-209 (504 retries), acct-REDACT-330 (failed calls).

iris: I'm starting a rolling drain of the most-affected nodes to stop new traffic landing: `redwoodctl node drain usw2-gpu-12 --reason "oom-cuda-frag" --duration 30m`

incident-bot: @here Runbook step triggered: "Graceful drain -> restart runtime -> monitor eviction". Please add notes when you complete each step.

alex: doing a targeted restart of runtime on drained nodes after drain complete. will also bump `KV_CACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD` to 0.6 for the pool to force more aggressive reclaim.

sana: please hold on the env tweak until we can validate it in one node. we don't want to thrash hot cache and increase tail latency. canary first.

dmitri: canary done on `usw2-gpu-12` — restarted runtime, applied `KV_CACHE_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.6`. preliminary metrics: free pages rose from 420MiB -> 1.1GiB over 40s.

megan: Customer comms update: support notified affected customers, suggested retry/backoff changes. No SLA breach expected yet but monitoring closely.

iris: I also kicked off a one-off defrag job on that node: `allocator-tool defrag --slab 12 --max-moves 200000` — it completed without errors, reclaimed ~380MiB.

alex: curious note — nvml shows inconsistent memory reported vs kernel: `nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo: total=16GiB free=2GiB used=14GiB` but kernel allocation failure claimed only 512MiB available. suspect internal fragmentation and per-process accounting mismatch.

sana: that may explain CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS — corrupted allocator metadata causing illegal mem access. we should avoid forcing new allocations on suspect nodes.

dmitri: agree. I'm labeling nodes `kv-frag-suspect=true` and setting scheduler taint `kv-frag=true` to prevent new pods from scheduling.

incident-bot: ACTIONS: drained 3 nodes, restarted runtime on 2 nodes (canary), defrag job run, taints applied to 4 nodes.

megan: ops ask: do we enable a temporary fallback to smaller model variant on affected routes to reduce memory footprint? Prod routes: `/v1/gen/text` and `/v1/chat/stream`.

alex: yes, rolling rollback to quantized-qa-small on affected routes makes sense. I'll trigger a canary rollout: `redwoodctl rollout set model gen-text -> quantized-qa-small --percent 10`

sana: confirm we have Eval coverage for quality drop? we should ensure critical customers aren't routed incorrectly.

dmitri: monitoring shows request latency normalizing on the canaries. eviction rate decreased. No new OOMs on nodes we fixed.

iris: re: customer impact: acct-REDACT-113 reported 40% failed requests during 21:50-22:05 UTC. support has the raw request ids.

megan: I'm drafting a post-incident note for comms. TLDR: gradual KV/page fragmentation led to allocator metadata drift -> illegal CUDA allocations -> pods crash -> node bounce. Mitigations: drain+restart+defrag, taint nodes, apply canary evict threshold, fallback to smaller model for affected traffic.

alex: root cause hypothesis: a long-running workload pattern (many short-lived sequences with irregular KV cache churn) combined with newer allocator change that reduced coalescing. will open PR to revert coalescing patch for now.

sana: next steps: 1) continue to monitor node pool for 2 hours, 2) schedule full fleet defrag during low traffic window, 3) revert allocator change in canary branch and run extended load test.

dmitri: I'll file an incident ticket with logs and flamegraphs: INC-2057. tagging infra/realtime/runtime.

iris: done with active live mitigation — nodes stabilized, traffic redirected off suspects, customers see decreasing error rates. moving to post-mortem channel in 30m. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Please add timeline + artifacts to INC-2057 and close this thread when postmortem note is published.

megan: thanks all. I'll capture customer-visible timeline and attach sample request ids.

alex: good catch by monitoring alert. we should consider adding fragmentation heuristics to alerting (stale_page_count > 1000 && slab_frag_percent > 70) so we detect earlier.

sana: agreed. also add a runbook step for `allocator-tool defrag` and `taint->drain` sequence.

(ends at 2057002968)
